\begin{abstract}
Latent world models that plan with short-horizon shooting become myopic
when the goal lies beyond one plan. We present FaBLeWM (Forward and
Backward LeWM). The official LeWorldModel (LeWM) encoder,
action-conditioned predictor, and 25-step cross-entropy method (CEM)
planner are left unchanged. Two action-free imaginers, trained on
detached latents, extend the cost that ranks CEM candidates: a forward
map continues from the predicted endpoint, and a backward map walks the
goal back toward it. Imagination is used only when the remaining time
to the goal exceeds one planning horizon. On PushT and TwoRoom
($n{=}50$, shared starts, epoch-10 checkpoint, CEM horizon $5$),
FaBLeWM matches Official LeWM at goal offset $25$ and raises success at
offsets $50$--$100$. On TwoRoom, Official already reaches $90\%$ at
offset $25$ and then falls to $50/32/18$; Forward stays at $90/84/66$.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

A learned latent world model is often paired with a short-horizon
planner. LeWorldModel~\citep{lewm2026} instantiates a joint-embedding
predictive architecture~\citep{lecun2022jepa} as an action-conditioned
world model: an encoder $E$ maps observations to latents, a predictor
$P$ rolls those latents forward under actions, and CEM~\citep{rubinstein1999cem}
selects a 25-step action sequence by the distance between the predicted
endpoint and a goal embedding. That loop is enough when the goal is
inside one planning horizon. It is not enough when the goal is $50$,
$75$, or $100$ steps away. CEM still emits 25-step plans; it ranks them
by how close a near-term endpoint sits to a still-distant goal.
Official success then drops, even if the same controller is reliable at
offset $25$.

FaBLeWM keeps Official LeWM---the encoder, the predictor, SIGReg, and
the 25-step planner---and extends the cost that ranks candidate plans.
Two action-free networks, a forward imaginer $F$ and a backward
imaginer $B$, are trained on stop-gradient latents and update only
themselves. At evaluation, $F$ continues from the predicted endpoint
and $B$ walks the goal backward. When the remaining time to the goal
fits in one CEM plan, both maps are bypassed and the cost is Official.
When it does not, CEM still plans 25 steps and scores them after $k$
imaginer steps.

On PushT and TwoRoom, with $50$ shared starts per task and the epoch-10
checkpoint, the four modes coincide at offset $25$ and diverge later.
On PushT, Backward reaches $70\%$ at offset $50$ (Official $44\%$) and
Forward is stronger at $75$ and $100$; averaging the two costs is the
best mid-range mix. On TwoRoom, Official is already at $90\%$ for
offset $25$, then $50/32/18$. Forward stays at $90/84/66$. A paired
comparison at offset $50$ saves $21$ Official failures and loses one
success. On PushT, $F$ and $B$ stay near the encoder's BatchNorm
sphere; on TwoRoom their output norms are lower, and Forward still
raises long-offset success.

\paragraph{Contributions.}
(i)~Detached forward and backward imaginers on an unchanged LeWM path.
(ii)~A CEM cost that applies $k$-step imagination only when the goal
lies beyond one plan, and reduces to Official when $k{=}0$.
(iii)~PushT and TwoRoom results in which the same 25-step CEM reaches
farther goals.

\section{Related work}
\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Latent world models and short-horizon CEM.}
PlaNet~\citep{hafner2019planet} and Dreamer~\citep{hafner2020dreamer}
learn dynamics in a latent space and plan by imagination.
TD-MPC~\citep{hansen2022tdmpc}, DINO-WM~\citep{zhou2025dinowm}, and
LeWM~\citep{lewm2026} score action sequences with CEM or a close
variant, typically by Euclidean distance between a predicted terminal
latent and a goal embedding. JEPA~\citep{lecun2022jepa} predicts in
representation space; LeWM is an action-conditioned JEPA world model
with SIGReg on the encoder. FaBLeWM uses that Official path as the
backbone: the same $E$, $P$, 25-step CEM, and terminal MSE.

\paragraph{Longer action-conditioned predictors.}
Variable-Length Latent World Models~\citep{du2026vlwm} train $P$ to
map a state and an action sequence of length $k$ directly to
$z_{t+k}$, with a curriculum over $k$, so the planner can query
horizons other than one-step rollouts. FaBLeWM leaves Official $P$ at
its trained one-step (action-block) scale and applies an
\emph{action-free} map after the 25-step CEM endpoint.

\paragraph{Hierarchy and subgoals.}
HWM~\citep{zhang2026hwm} trains world models at several temporal
resolutions in a shared latent space; high-level predictions become
subgoals for short-horizon MPC, with a learned action encoder for
macro-actions. FF-JEPA~\citep{masip2026ffjepa} adds an action-free
forward latent planner that proposes the next subgoal; CEM then
reaches that subgoal with the action-conditioned model, and the
setting is goal-free. SAGE~\citep{cheng2026sage} keeps a frozen
LeWM and CEM budget, predicts a reachable latent subgoal at a
requested duration, and uses it to condition the action
\emph{proposals} that CEM refines. FaBLeWM keeps a single flat 25-step
CEM against the given goal image. $F$ and $B$ change the arguments of
the terminal cost, not the subgoal that CEM tracks and not the
proposal distribution.

\paragraph{CEM cost and latent metrics.}
The default CEM cost in this line of work is terminal Euclidean
MSE~\citep{lewm2026,zhou2025dinowm,hansen2022tdmpc}. That cost is
fragile when latent geometry and reachability disagree. Temporal
straightening~\citep{wang2026straightening} regularizes encoder
trajectories so Euclidean distance better matches geodesic progress.
Trajectory reachability metrics~\citep{li2026trm} keep $E$, $P$, and
CEM fixed and replace or mix the terminal cost with a pairwise head
trained on horizon-matched temporal separations; on a hard TwoRoom
setting this ranking repair is the difference between collapse and
high success. FaBLeWM also keeps Euclidean MSE and the Official
dynamics. It changes \emph{which} pair the MSE sees: $\Fk(\Pend)$
versus $\zg$, or $\Pend$ versus $\Bk(\zg)$, with $k$ set by the
remaining time beyond one plan. The metric stays MSE; the compared
latents are brought onto a common horizon.

\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\subsection{Official LeWM}
\label{sec:official}

We use the official LeWM training path. A window of four encoded
observations $z_{0:3}=E(o_{0:3})$ and the corresponding actions is fed
to $P$. Prediction targets are the encoder latents. The loss is
next-embedding MSE plus SIGReg,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{official}}
=\underbrace{\|P(z,a)-z_{\mathrm{next}}\|^2}_{\mathrm{pred}}
+0.09\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SIGReg}}(z).
\end{equation}
At evaluation, CEM always plans $\planlen$ environment steps
(horizon $5$, receding horizon $5$, action block $5$). Official cost is
$\|\Pend-\zg\|^2$, where $\Pend$ is the predicted embedding after those
$25$ steps.

\subsection{Detached imaginers}
\label{sec:imaginers}

Forward $F$ and Backward $B$ are residual MLPs on a single latent.
They read stop-gradient copies of $z$ and of $P$'s output $p$, so
imaginer losses train only $F$ and $B$. With a four-step window,
$p_1,p_2,p_3$ align with $z_1,z_2,z_3$.

\paragraph{Forward.}
$F$ is trained to map a predicted latent to a later encoder latent,
\begin{equation}
F(p_1)\to z_2,\qquad F(p_2)\to z_3,\qquad F(F(p_1))\to z_3,
\end{equation}
with equal weight on the one-step and two-step terms. At evaluation,
\begin{equation}
C_F=\bigl\|\Fk(\Pend)-\zg\bigr\|^2.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Backward.}
Unary Backward maps encoder latents, $B(z)\to z$:
\begin{equation}
B(z_3)\to z_2,\qquad B(z_2)\to z_1,\qquad B(B(z_3))\to z_1.
\end{equation}
At evaluation,
\begin{equation}
C_B=\bigl\|\Pend-\Bk(\zg)\bigr\|^2.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Imagination depth.}
For goal offset $o$ and elapsed time $t$,
\begin{equation}
k=\max\bigl((o-t-\planlen)/5,\,0\bigr).
\end{equation}
The division by $5$ matches the action block, so $k$ counts imaginer
steps. When $k{=}0$, $F$ and $B$ are bypassed and
$C_F=C_B=\|\Pend-\zg\|^2$. At offset $25$ the first replan has
$k{=}0$, so Official, Forward, Backward, and Fusion share the same cost.

\paragraph{Fusion.}
Unless noted, Fusion is a uniform mix
$C=0.5\,C_F+0.5\,C_B$ (avg05). CEM, the action space, and the 25-step
horizon are shared by Official, Forward, Backward, and Fusion.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:exp}

We evaluate four planning modes on the same frozen checkpoint: Official,
Forward, Backward, and Fusion (avg05). Each task uses $n{=}50$ episodes,
evaluation seed $42$, and a shared set of start states. Checkpoints are
taken at epoch $10$. CEM uses horizon $5$ at every offset. Success is
the environment criterion. PushT~\citep{florence2022ibc}
uses checkpoint \texttt{fblewm}; TwoRoom uses
\texttt{fblewm\_tworoom}. Both train unary $B\to z$.

\subsection{PushT}
\label{sec:pusht}

Table~\ref{tab:pusht} reports PushT. At offset $25$ all four modes are
at $82\%$. At longer offsets Backward reaches $70\%$ at $50$
($+26$ vs.\ Official), Forward is stronger at $75$ and $100$, and
Fusion is the best mid-range mix ($78\%$ and $50\%$ at $50$ and $75$),
with $18\%$ at offset $100$ (Official $12\%$).

\begin{table}[htbp]
\caption{PushT success (\%). CEM horizon $5$ at all offsets. Same $50$ starts.
Checkpoint \texttt{fblewm}, unary $B\to z$.}
\label{tab:pusht}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
Mode & 25 & 50 & 75 & 100 \\
\hline \\
Official        & 82 & 44 & 22 & 12 \\
Forward         & 82 & 62 & 42 & 28 \\
Backward        & 82 & 70 & 34 & 10 \\
Fusion (avg05)  & 82 & 78 & 50 & 18 \\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\end{table}

Figure~\ref{fig:pusht-train} shows validation losses and latent norms.
SIGReg is calm from epoch $0$. By epoch $9$, Forward and Backward
outputs sit at about $13.0$ against encoder targets of about $13.8$,
near the BatchNorm sphere $\sqrt{192}\approx 13.9$.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=0.98\linewidth]{figures/fig_pusht_train.png}
\end{center}
\caption{PushT validation losses and latent norms over $10$ epochs.
Official is $\mathrm{pred}+0.09\cdot\mathrm{SIGReg}$. Forward and
Backward stay near the BatchNorm sphere
($\Vert z\Vert\approx\sqrt{192}\approx 13.9$).}
\label{fig:pusht-train}
\end{figure}

\FloatBarrier

\subsection{TwoRoom}
\label{sec:tworoom}

On TwoRoom (Table~\ref{tab:tworoom}, Figure~\ref{fig:tworoom-success}),
Official is at $90\%$ for offset $25$, then $50/32/18$ at
$50/75/100$. Forward matches Official at offset $25$ (the same five
episodes fail) and then stays at $90/84/66$: $+40$, $+52$, and
$+48$ points. At offset $50$, on the same starts, Forward saves $21$
Official failures and loses one Official success. Backward adds $+4$
to $+8$ points after offset $25$. Fusion lies between Forward and
Official. The 25-step CEM is already competent at short range; $\Fk$
re-scores the same candidates against $\zg$ after $k$ imaginer steps.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\caption{TwoRoom success (\%). CEM horizon $5$ at all offsets. Same $50$ starts.
Checkpoint \texttt{fblewm\_tworoom}, unary $B\to z$.}
\label{tab:tworoom}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
Mode & 25 & 50 & 75 & 100 \\
\hline \\
Official        & 90 & 50 & 32 & 18 \\
Forward         & 90 & 90 & 84 & 66 \\
Backward        & 92 & 54 & 40 & 24 \\
Fusion (avg05)  & 90 & 76 & 58 & 32 \\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=0.98\linewidth]{figures/fig_tworoom_success.png}
\end{center}
\caption{TwoRoom success (\%) vs.\ goal offset. Official, Forward,
Backward, and Fusion (avg05) share 25-step CEM. Official is strong at
offset $25$ and drops at longer offsets; Forward stays high. Fusion
lies between Forward and Official.}
\label{fig:tworoom-success}
\end{figure}

Figure~\ref{fig:tworoom-train} starts at epoch $0$. SIGReg is $61.5$
then $51.2$ in the first two epochs, and then falls as the encoder
moves onto the sphere. After that, $F$ and $B$ outputs stay near
$5.6$ while their targets sit near $13.7$. CEM orders candidates by
these imagined latents. On PushT the output norms stay near the
encoder sphere; on TwoRoom they do not. Forward raises long-offset
success in both cases.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=0.98\linewidth]{figures/fig_tworoom_train.png}
\end{center}
\caption{TwoRoom validation losses and latent norms, including epochs
$0$--$1$. SIGReg spikes, then the encoder settles on the BatchNorm
sphere. Forward and Backward outputs remain at about $5.6$ against
targets of about $13.7$.}
\label{fig:tworoom-train}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Scope}
\label{sec:limits}

The reported runs are unary $B\to z$ on PushT and TwoRoom, at the
epoch-10 checkpoint. Fusion is the best mid-range mix on PushT and
lies below Forward on TwoRoom. PushT success at offset $100$ is
$18\%$ under Fusion.

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:concl}

FaBLeWM keeps Official LeWM's encoder, predictor, and 25-step CEM, and
adds detached forward and backward imaginers that re-score those plans.
On PushT and TwoRoom, Official and FaBLeWM match at offset $25$, where
$k{=}0$, and FaBLeWM raises success at longer offsets, where CEM ranks
25-step plans that do not reach the goal.

\section{Protocol details}
\label{app:protocol}

CEM uses \texttt{horizon=5}, \texttt{receding=5}, and
\texttt{action\_block=5}, so one plan is $\planlen$ environment steps.
Imagination depth is $k=\max((o-t-25)/5,\,0)$. Official cost is
$\|\Pend-\zg\|^2$; Forward is $\|\Fk(\Pend)-\zg\|^2$; unary Backward is
$\|\Pend-\Bk(\zg)\|^2$; Fusion (avg05) is the mean of the last two.
When $k{=}0$, Forward and Backward are skipped.

PushT starts hash:
\texttt{9d47d5e78eb0b98693bdb739e6e107fca7b52a7fa5d38189e418c242d7d2a703}.
TwoRoom starts hash:
\texttt{55d795562181c8f5eb12def43fb995cedd0d45c909fd1f39e38518155e16ad80}.

On TwoRoom at offset $50$, Forward vs.\ Official on the same $50$
starts: $21$ episodes saved, $1$ lost. Official and Forward at offset
$25$ fail on the same five episodes.
